kt_docs.body:
# Knowledge Transfer — Aarav Mehta (Payments Platform)

## System Overview
The Payments Microservices Platform consists of four Spring Boot services:
`payment-orchestrator`, `ledger-service`, `refund-worker`, and the
`payments-bff`. They communicate over REST and an internal Kafka topic
(`payments.events`). Data is stored in PostgreSQL (`paydb`) with read replicas.

## Architecture Notes
- `payment-orchestrator` is the entry point; it coordinates authorization,
  capture, and settlement via a state machine.
- Idempotency is enforced using a Redis-backed idempotency key store.
- The Acme Retail client portal calls the BFF, never the services directly.

## Pending Tickets & In-Flight Work
- PAY-1423: Retry storm on refund-worker under high load — mitigation in review.
- PAY-1451: Migrate ledger-service to the new currency-rounding library.
- PAY-1460: Acme Retail requested a new partial-refund flow (design phase).

## Key Contacts
- Product: Riya Sen (payments PM)
- Client: Acme Retail integration team (integrations@acme-retail.example)
- On-call rotation: shared payments PagerDuty schedule.

## Business Logic Caveats
- Settlement batches run at 02:00 IST; do not deploy between 01:30-02:30.
- The `ledger-service` reconciliation job must not be run twice in a day.

## Open Questions for Successor
- Ownership of the partial-refund design (PAY-1460) needs to be reassigned.

> NOTE: This KT does not yet include a Deployment / Runbook section describing
> how to build, deploy, roll back, and operate these services. Reviewer to
> flag as a gap.

kt_docs.body:
# Knowledge Transfer — Dev Patel (Cloud Infrastructure & CI/CD)

## System Overview
The AWS environment is a multi-account landing zone managed with Terraform
(state in an S3 backend with DynamoDB locking). Accounts: `mgmt`, `shared`,
`prod`, `staging`, `dev`. Networking uses a Transit Gateway hub.

## Terraform / IaC Notes
- Root module lives in the `infra-live` repo; modules in `infra-modules`.
- `terraform plan` must be run against the `prod` workspace with the
  `prod-deployer` role. Never apply from a laptop; use the pipeline.
- State is locked per-workspace; a stuck lock can be released via the DynamoDB
  `terraform-locks` table.

## CI/CD Platform
- GitHub Actions with self-hosted runners in the `shared` account.
- Deployment pipelines gate on the `staging` smoke tests before `prod`.

## Deployment / Runbook
- To deploy infra: open PR to `infra-live`, pipeline runs plan, requires one
  approval, then apply on merge.
- Rollback: revert the merge commit; the pipeline re-applies the previous state.
- Incident runbook: check CloudWatch dashboard `platform-overview`, then
  PagerDuty for the triggering alarm.

## Pending Tickets & In-Flight Work
- OPS-882: Transit Gateway route cleanup for the decommissioned `legacy` VPC.
- OPS-905: Upgrade EKS node groups to the latest AMI.
- OPS-910: Migrate CI secrets from the old vault path.

## Key Contacts
- Engineering Manager: Vikram Sharma
- Security: CISO office for any IAM policy changes.

> NOTE: This KT does not include an Access & Credentials handover section. The
> owner holds broad privileged access (AWS admin roles, CI/CD secrets,
> PagerDuty admin) and the specific credentials, secret locations, and rotation
> steps are NOT documented here. Reviewer to flag this as a critical gap given
> this is a termination case.

kt_docs.title: kt-003
kt_docs.body:
# Knowledge Transfer — Karthik Nair (Notifications & Ingestion)

## System Overview
Two systems: the **Notifications Service** (Kafka-driven fan-out to email/SMS/
push) and the **Data Ingestion Pipeline** (nightly ETL from client systems into
Snowflake).

## Notifications Service
- Consumes the `notifications.requested` Kafka topic.
- Providers: SES (email), a third-party SMS gateway, and FCM (push).
- Templates are stored in the `notif-templates` repo and rendered at send time.
- Rate limiting is per-tenant, configured in the `notif-config` table.

## Data Ingestion Pipeline
- Airflow DAG `client_ingest_nightly` runs at 01:00 IST.
- Extracts from client SFTP drops, validates schema, loads into Snowflake
  `RAW` schema, then dbt transforms into `ANALYTICS`.
- Failure alerts post to the `#data-alerts` Slack channel.

## Deployment / Runbook
- Both services deploy via the standard GitHub Actions pipeline.
- Rollback: redeploy the previous image tag from the registry.
- Airflow DAG can be manually re-triggered from the Airflow UI after fixing the
  upstream data issue.

## Access & Credentials Handover
- SES sending is via an IAM role, not personal keys; hand over via team role.
- Snowflake access is through the `analytics_loader` service account (secret in
  the team vault path `secret/data/snowflake`).
- FCM server key rotation instructions are in the `notif-config` README.

## Key Contacts
- Data PM: Rohit Bhatt
- Analytics consumers: Finance reporting team.

> NOTE: This KT does not include a Pending Tickets / In-Flight Work section.
> Open Jira items, half-finished migrations, and any in-progress client
> onboarding are NOT listed. Reviewer to flag as a gap.

# Exit Interview — Rahul Verma (Sales)

**Reason for leaving:**
Primarily burnout and frustration with sales leadership. Quotas were raised
twice in one year without any change in territory support or lead flow. I felt
set up to fail regardless of effort.

**What you liked:**
The product is genuinely good and my peers on the AE team were supportive. Some
of the enterprise clients were a pleasure to work with.

**What could improve:**
Sales management is the biggest issue. Targets are set top-down with no input,
pipeline reviews turned into blame sessions, and there was constant pressure but
little coaching. Commission plan changes were communicated late and felt unfair.
High attrition on the team is a symptom of this.

**Manager feedback:**
My manager (Karan) is under pressure himself and passes it straight down. Very
little one-on-one support or career development. Micromanaged on activity
metrics while ignoring actual deal blockers.

**Would you recommend Perficient as a place to work?**
Not in the Sales org as it currently runs. Maybe in Engineering or Product.

**What could improve:**
Same theme as others on the team: leadership sets aggressive targets without

same reasons in the last few months.

**Manager feedback:**
Karan is knowledgeable but stretched thin. One-on-ones were often cancelled and

demotivating.

**Would you recommend Perficient as a place to work?**
For the company overall, maybe. For the Sales development team, not right now
until the management and quota culture changes.

policies.title: Company Asset Return Policy
policies.body:
# Company Asset Return Policy

## 1. Purpose
1.1 To ensure timely and complete recovery of all company-issued assets from
separating employees.

## 2. Assets in Scope
2.1 Computing devices — laptops (MacBook Pro/Air), desktops.
2.2 Mobile devices — company iPhones and tablets.
2.3 Security hardware — YubiKeys, access cards.
2.4 Peripherals — monitors, docking stations, keyboards.
2.5 Any other company property (books, corporate credit cards, ID badge).

## 3. Return Timeline
3.1 Assets must be returned **on or before the last working day**.
3.2 For remote employees, IT arranges a prepaid shipping kit; assets must be
dispatched no later than the last working day and received within 7 days.
3.3 Failure to return assets may result in recovery deductions from the
full-and-final settlement.

## 4. Condition & Inspection
4.1 Returned devices are inspected and logged against the assets_assigned record
in the employee profile.
4.2 Damage beyond normal wear may be recovered at depreciated value.

## 5. Data Handling
5.1 Devices are backed up (where required) and then securely wiped per the IT
Deprovisioning Policy before reissue.

## 6. Sign-off
6.1 A completed asset return checklist is required to close the IT Clearance
stage of the exit case.
6.2 Any outstanding assets are flagged to Finance to hold settlement.

## 7. Recovery Valuation Table (indicative)
| Asset | Standard Recovery Value (unreturned) |
|-------|--------------------------------------|
| MacBook Pro 16" | INR 180,000 |
| MacBook Pro 14" | INR 150,000 |
| MacBook Air 13" | INR 95,000 |
| iPhone 14 | INR 70,000 |
| YubiKey | INR 4,000 |
| 27" Monitor | INR 22,000 |

policies.title: Data Retention, Confidentiality & NDA Policy
policies.body:
# Data Retention, Confidentiality & NDA Policy

## 1. Purpose
1.1 To define confidentiality obligations that survive employment and the
retention/disposal rules for company and client data at separation.

## 2. Surviving Confidentiality Obligations
2.1 The Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) signed at joining remains binding
indefinitely after separation.
2.2 Separating employees must not retain, copy, or transmit any confidential,
proprietary, or client data.
2.3 A signed **Confidentiality Reaffirmation** is collected during HR Clearance.

## 3. Data Return & Deletion
3.1 All company data on personal devices must be deleted; the employee attests
to this in writing.
3.2 Client deliverables and source code remain the property of Perficient and/or
its clients and must be handed over during Knowledge Transfer.

## 4. Retention Schedule
4.1 Employee HR records — retained **7 years** after separation.
4.2 Payroll and tax records (PF/TDS) — retained **8 years** per statutory rules.
4.3 Email mailbox — retained **30 days** as forwarding, then archived for
**1 year**, then deleted.
4.4 Access and deprovisioning audit logs — retained **12 months**.

## 5. Intellectual Property
5.1 All work product created during employment is company IP.
5.2 Personal projects unrelated to company business are excluded per the IP
assignment clause of the employment agreement.

## 6. Breach Handling
6.1 Suspected breaches of confidentiality post-exit are referred to Legal &
Compliance and may result in legal action.

## 7. Cross-References
7.1 Asset and credential handling are governed by the IT Deprovisioning Policy.
7.2 Retention of settlement records is coordinated with Finance.

policies.title: Employee Offboarding & Exit SLA Policy
policies.body:
# Employee Offboarding & Exit SLA Policy

## 1. Purpose
1.1 This policy governs the end-to-end offboarding of any employee separating
from Perficient, whether by resignation, termination, or retirement.
1.2 It defines the mandatory clearance stages, service-level agreements (SLAs),
and escalation rules to ensure timely, secure, and compliant exits.

## 2. Scope
2.1 Applies to all employees and contractors across Engineering, Finance, HR,
Sales, and IT.
2.2 Covers the period from resignation/termination acceptance through the final
full-and-final settlement.

## 3. Offboarding Stages
Every exit case must progress through the following five stages:
3.1 **IT Clearance** — Deprovisioning of all system access and recovery of
assets. Owner: IT Systems Administration.
3.2 **Finance Clearance** — Settlement of dues, recovery of advances, and
full-and-final calculation. Owner: Finance.
3.3 **HR Clearance** — Documentation, exit interview, and relieving letter.
Owner: HR Business Partner.
3.4 **Knowledge Transfer** — Handover of responsibilities, documentation, and
credentials to designated owners. Owner: Reporting Manager.
3.5 **Manager Sign-off** — Final confirmation that all deliverables and
handovers are complete. Owner: Reporting Manager.

## 4. Service-Level Agreements (SLA)
4.1 Each stage must be **completed within five (5) business days** of being
opened.
4.2 A stage is considered **OVERDUE** when its `days_open` exceeds 5.
4.3 The overall exit case must reach completion no later than the employee's
last working day, except where Finance Clearance depends on the final payroll
cycle.

## 5. Escalation Rules
5.1 **Level 1 (Day 6):** An overdue stage triggers an automated reminder to the
stage owner and the reporting manager.
5.2 **Level 2 (Day 8):** The department head is notified and the case is flagged
`at_risk`.
5.3 **Level 3 (Day 10):** Escalation to the HR Director. For any open IT
Clearance involving production or privileged access, the CISO is also notified.
5.4 Termination cases and cases involving high-criticality resources are
escalated one level earlier than the timelines above.

## 6. Roles & Responsibilities
6.1 The reporting manager is accountable for overall case completion.
6.2 HR Operations owns this policy and monitors SLA compliance across all cases.
6.3 Stage owners are responsible for updating case status promptly.

## 7. Exceptions
7.1 SLA extensions require written approval from the HR Director.
7.2 Exceptions must be logged in the exit case timeline notes.

policies.title: IT Deprovisioning & Access Revocation Policy
policies.body:
# IT Deprovisioning & Access Revocation Policy

## 1. Purpose
1.1 To ensure that all system access, credentials, and hardware assigned to a
separating employee are revoked and recovered in a secure, auditable manner.

## 2. Timing
2.1 For **resignations**, access revocation is scheduled to complete by end of
the last working day.
2.2 For **terminations**, all access must be revoked **immediately** upon
notification, before the employee is informed where legally permissible.
2.3 Privileged/production access (AWS admin, CI/CD secrets, database root,
PagerDuty) must be revoked within **4 hours** of case initiation.

## 3. Systems Checklist
3.1 Identity provider (Okta/SSO) — disable account, revoke active sessions.
3.2 Source control (GitHub) — remove from all orgs and teams; rotate any shared
deploy keys the user could access.
3.3 Cloud (AWS) — remove IAM user/role bindings; rotate access keys.
3.4 Business apps — Salesforce, SAP, Workday, Jira, Confluence.
3.5 Network — VPN certificate revocation and MFA/YubiKey deactivation.
3.6 Email — convert to a shared/forwarding mailbox for 30 days, then archive.

## 4. Credential Rotation
4.1 Any shared secret, service-account password, or API key known to the
employee must be rotated within 24 hours of exit.
4.2 Rotation is mandatory for all privileged users regardless of exit type.

## 5. Asset Recovery
5.1 All company hardware (laptop, phone, YubiKey, monitors) must be returned and
logged. See the Asset Return Policy for details.
5.2 Endpoints are remotely wiped after data backup confirmation.

## 6. Audit & Evidence
6.1 A deprovisioning checklist is completed and attached to the exit case.
6.2 Revocation timestamps are retained for 12 months for audit.

## 7. Dependencies
7.1 Where deprovisioning is blocked by an incomplete Knowledge Transfer, the
dependency and its risk must be recorded in the case timeline and escalated per
the Exit SLA Policy.

# Documents & Forms Required at Each Exit Stage

Use this checklist to prepare the documents needed to complete each clearance
stage without delays.

## 1. At Resignation / Notice
- Resignation letter (via Workday).
- Acknowledgement of notice period.
- Updated personal contact details and personal email for post-exit
  correspondence.

## 2. Knowledge Transfer Stage
- **KT document** (submitted in the KT system) covering:
  - Deployment / runbook procedures
  - Access & credentials handover list
  - Pending tickets and in-flight work
  - Key contacts and vendor details
- Successor acknowledgement (signed by the receiving team member).

## 3. IT Clearance Stage
- **Asset Return Checklist** (signed by IT).
- Device handover acknowledgement.
- VPN/MFA deactivation confirmation.

## 4. Finance Clearance Stage
- No-dues declaration.
- Advance/loan settlement confirmation (if applicable).
- Bank account confirmation for FnF credit.
- Form 16 request (issued after year-end).

## 5. HR Clearance Stage
- Completed **exit interview** form.
- Signed **Confidentiality Reaffirmation** (NDA survival).
- ID badge and access card return acknowledgement.
- PF transfer/withdrawal form (Form 19 / Form 10C or UAN transfer).

## 6. On Final Sign-off
- **Relieving letter** (issued by HR).
- **Experience letter** (issued by HR).
- Full-and-final settlement statement (issued by Finance).

## Notes
- Missing documents are the most common cause of overdue stages.
- Digital signatures are accepted for all forms except statutory PF forms where
  a wet signature may be required.

# Exit Process Overview

This guide explains what an exiting employee at Perficient goes through, the
typical timeline, and who to contact at each step.

## Step 1 — Resignation / Notice (Day 0)
- Submit your resignation to your reporting manager and HR via Workday.
- Standard notice period is **60 days** for full-time employees (30 days for
  employees with under 1 year of tenure).
- HR acknowledges and creates an **exit case** with five clearance stages.
- **Contact:** your reporting manager and your HR Business Partner.

## Step 2 — Knowledge Transfer (Weeks 1-3)
- Work with your manager to identify successors and document your work.
- Submit a Knowledge Transfer (KT) document covering deployment/runbooks,
  access & credentials, pending tickets, and key contacts.
- KT is reviewed by your manager and must be marked complete before IT
  deprovisioning of production access.
- **Contact:** reporting manager.

## Step 3 — IT Clearance (Last week)
- Return all assets (laptop, phone, YubiKey, monitors).
- System access is revoked per the IT Deprovisioning Policy; each stage targets
  completion within **5 business days**.
- **Contact:** IT Systems Administration (Sanya Kapoor).

## Step 4 — Finance Clearance (Around last working day)
- Any advances or dues are settled; full-and-final (FnF) is calculated.
- FnF is credited within **45 days** of the last working day.
- **Contact:** Finance / Payroll (Pooja Shah).

## Step 5 — HR Clearance & Documents (Last week)
- Complete the exit interview.
- Sign the confidentiality reaffirmation.
- Receive your **relieving and experience letters** after final sign-off.
- **Contact:** HR Business Partner (Meera Krishnan).

## Step 6 — Manager Sign-off (Final)
- Your manager confirms all handovers and deliverables are complete.
- Once all five stages are complete, the exit case is closed.

## SLA & Escalation
- Each stage must complete within 5 business days; overdue stages are escalated
  per the Exit SLA Policy. If a stage stalls, contact HR Operations.

process_docs.title: Exit FAQ (Source for Chatbot)
process_docs.body:
# Exit FAQ

Common questions and answers about separation from Perficient. This document is
the source of truth for the offboarding FAQ chatbot.

## Notice Period
**Q: What is the standard notice period?**
A: 60 days for employees with 1+ year of tenure, 30 days for those under 1 year.

**Q: Can I buy out my notice period?**
A: Notice buyout is possible with manager and HR approval; the buyout amount is
recovered from your full-and-final settlement.

## Full-and-Final Settlement
**Q: When will I receive my full-and-final (FnF) settlement?**
A: FnF is processed and credited within **45 days** of your last working day,
subject to completion of all clearances and asset returns.

**Q: What does FnF include?**
A: Unpaid salary, leave encashment for eligible balance, any pending
reimbursements, minus recoveries (notice buyout, advances, unreturned assets).

## Experience & Relieving Letters
**Q: When do I get my relieving and experience letters?**
A: Both are issued by HR after the Manager Sign-off stage is complete, typically
within 3 business days of case closure.

**Q: Can I get the experience letter earlier for a background check?**
A: An employment verification letter can be requested from HR at any time; the
formal experience letter is issued at exit.

## Provident Fund (PF)
**Q: What happens to my PF?**
A: You can transfer your PF to your new employer via your UAN, or withdraw it.
HR provides the required forms during HR Clearance.

**Q: How long does PF transfer take?**
A: PF transfers typically take 15-30 days once the withdrawal/transfer form is
submitted to EPFO.

## Insurance
**Q: Does my health insurance continue after exit?**
A: Group medical insurance coverage ends on your last working day. A conversion
option to an individual policy may be available; contact HR for details.

## Access & Assets
**Q: When does my system access get revoked?**
A: Access is revoked by end of your last working day (immediately for
terminations). Return all assets on or before your last working day.

**Q: What if I can't return my laptop in time?**
A: Contact IT for a prepaid shipping kit. Unreturned assets may be recovered
from your settlement at depreciated value.

## Escalation
**Q: My clearance is stuck. What do I do?**
A: Each stage should complete within 5 business days. If overdue, contact HR
Operations; overdue stages are automatically escalated to department heads.
